subject.title: fix(groq): keep default Llama agent turns within TPM limit

question: Should Groq TPM recovery remain an error-triggered provider policy, or should OpenAI-compatible transports stop treating discovered model output capability as the implicit reservation?
rationale: Both approaches can fix the reported HTTP 413, but they intentionally differ in successful-request output semantics, provider scope, tool availability during recovery, and compatibility blast radius.

options.title: Land provider-scoped recovery
options.body: Accept this PR's narrow, live-proven retry while explicitly owning the tool-free fallback and no recovery on older hosts without provenance.

options.title: Prefer transport-wide omission
options.body: Pause this PR and require https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/104916 to provide equivalent live-provider and upgrade proof before using the broader semantic change.

recommendation.title: Land provider-scoped recovery
recommendation.body: Accept this PR's narrow, live-proven retry while explicitly owning the tool-free fallback and no recovery on older hosts without provenance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the Agents runtime and provider/plugin ownership boundary assigned to this person in repository ownership documentation.
